prerequisite: Run survey_dredge_regions first to see each region's handle / name / crest elevation and trial volume, then set bottom_elev / slope_ratio_m / regions from that
fixture_requirements: >= 2 closed polylines on the boundary layer (with arc segments and concave corners)
One boundary drawn clockwise (verifies winding detection; the inward normal must not flip)
At least two regions using different slope ratios (verifies per-region overrides in regions)
At least one boundary partly outside the existing-ground surface (verifies the off_surface branch)
assertions: In-memory change only: results must be kept with an explicit save_dwg
surfaces == regions == number of closed polylines on the boundary layer (open ones are excluded)
One TIN per region named surface_prefix + id; a name clash gets a -2 suffix instead of silently overwriting someone else's surface
Design surface minimum elevation == bottom_elev (flat bottom); maximum == that region's z_top_max
The boundary polyline is the top-of-slope line: the design surface bounding box does not exceed the boundary bounding box (grading goes inward, never outward)
The same boundary drawn clockwise and counter-clockwise yields identical point elevations (winding is judged by signed area; Polyline.Area is always positive and cannot tell)
Toe points at concave corners stay inside the boundary: every toe point passes GridPointInPolygon and its distance to the boundary is >= 0.9 x the local band width
For any point on the design surface, elevation == max(bottom_elev, crest elevation - distance to boundary / m), within slope_step/m
regions match by exact handle first, then by label (text inside the region); only when neither matches are the global parameters used
Regions given slope_ratio_m in regions report the override in per_region.slope_ratio_m; the others report the global value
A handle/label named in regions that does not exist in the drawing goes to warnings and is not ignored silently
With start_elev the region's crest elevation is fixed around the whole ring (z_top_min == z_top_max == start_elev)
With start_elev_cap z_top_max <= cap while places below the cap still follow the terrain
Segments whose crest elevation is below bottom_elev have band == 0 and the design surface there == bottom_elev (no grading and no fill slope)
Boundary samples outside the existing-ground surface are treated as bottom_elev and reported in warnings (better to under-cut than to cut blindly)
band_max == (z_top_max - bottom_elev) x m
All grid points inside the slope band are kept; the flat bottom keeps only sparse flat_step points (vertex count matches slope_step/flat_step)
Halving slope_step changes the design surface volume by < 2% (convergence)

Outer-boundary clipping applies: design triangles never cross the boundary polyline; if the clipping API throws, that region gets a warning and falls back to convex-hull triangulation without failing the batch
With draw_crest_line=true each region gets one 3D crest line on crest_layer whose vertex elevations == the local crest elevation
With draw_toe_line=true and >= 3 toe points each region gets one 3D toe line on toe_layer with every vertex at bottom_elev
A fully flat region (no crest above the bottom elevation) draws no toe line, adds a warning and does not throw
Rerun with clear_existing=true removes only surfaces with the surface_prefix and lines carrying C3DF_DREDGE XData; user-drawn lines and other surfaces are untouched
Idempotent: two runs with the same parameters report the same surfaces/crest_lines/toe_lines and nothing stacks in the drawing
Rerun with clear_existing=false stacks (confirms the clearing switch really works)
Missing bottom_elev throws and names the parameter (never silently cuts to 0)
Missing or <= 0 slope_ratio_m throws; a region with slope_ratio_m <= 0 throws and names that region id
sample_step <= 0 / slope_step <= 0 throws
No closed polyline on the boundary layer throws and names the layer
The finished design surface can be edited by hand: downstream calculate_surface_volume reads the surface in the drawing, not this node's in-memory result
